short_title: Ferdinand to John II, Seville, 9 Jun 1478 (DARA C_CRAR/000001/0024)
writer: Prince Ferdinand (king of Castile, heir of Aragon)
recipient: John II of Aragon and Navarre
date: Seville, 9 Jun 1478 (dateline on p. 3 'De Sevilla ... de junio del anyo M CCCC lxxviii', read from image; DARA record 1478/06/09: https://dara.aragon.es/opac/app/item?i=1055720)
matters: Ferdinand's own cipher report to his father three weeks before the birth of Prince Juan (30 Jun 1478) and a month before John II's cipher letters of 10 Jul and 11 Aug 1478 on the prince's custody, the Castilian succession and the anti-French Trastamara league; the reply side of that exchange survives only in Zurita's summary and RAH copies, Ferdinand's side not read

neighbour_keys: Tomokiyo 2018 'Ferdinand-John II of Aragon Cipher (1476-1479)', Academia.edu 37751652 (https://www.academia.edu/37751652; key reconstructed, text not seen, 403); targets/ferdinand1473 key_1473.md and key_1474.md (outside repo; 1473/1474 systems, earlier, design differs by profile: 1473 letters+digits+crosses, 1474 bar and dotted signs)

notes: Pass on gate 4 rests on Tomokiyo's 1476-79 key being obtainable and of this system; if it is not, there is no pair and the item fails. Scans at sources/cache/cross/2854/. Long text (~2200 signs) makes it a good ciphertext-only bench if a key holds partly.

short_title: Juan Manuel to the Catholic Monarchs and Charles V, seven letters 1496-1522 (BNE MSS/20212/61/1-7)

matters: weak as stated: a Castilian envoy's cipher report from Genoa in Nov 1496, during the Holy League's war on French influence in Italy, would be among the oldest Spanish diplomatic ciphers of the Catholic Monarchs; what it reports is unknown and no study of the 1496 mission was found

short_title: Card. Giulio de' Medici to Galeotto de' Medici, Florence, May 1520/21, two bare letters in two sign ciphers (ASF MAP CXXXVII 733-734)
writer: Cardinal Giulio de' Medici, vice-chancellor (autograph 'V. Jul. vicecancell.')
recipient: Galeotto de' Medici, Medici agent in Rome
date: 734: 'Floren. xv Maij MDXXj' read from the image (A0001673, dateline at full size); 733 undated on recto; ASF record https://archiviodistatofirenze.cultura.gov.it/map/ricerca/ricerca-su-filza/?f=137&d=734&c=
matters: Outgoing cipher of the cardinal who governed Florence and directed Leo X's diplomacy, written in the weeks of the secret papal-imperial treaty of 8 May 1521 (or, if 1520, of his Florentine reform year); about 55 lines unread, no decipherment on file
matters_src: PRIMARY: ASF MAP images (above); SCHOLARLY: Dizionario Biografico degli Italiani, 'Clemente VII', https://www.treccani.it/enciclopedia/papa-clemente-vii_(Dizionario-Biografico)/ (legate in Tuscany 27 May 1519; treaty with Charles V 'datato 8 maggio ma rimasto per allora segreto'). Note: DBI has Giulio leaving for Florence 28 Jan 1521 and back 30 Apr, so a Florence dateline of 15 May 1521 needs checking against his itinerary
